description.purpose: Search Linear issues, projects, and cycles by free-text query and return ranked smart IDs.
when_to_use: When the user wants to find an issue by partial title, identifier (e.g. LIN-1234), or label.
When the exact issue id is unknown but team or project context is available.
when_not_to_use: When the exact identifier is already known — use `fetch` instead.
When enumerating every issue in a cycle — use `list_objects` with a filter.
limitations: Returns at most 50 results per call (Linear GraphQL pagination cap).
Free-text search runs against title and description; label/assignee filters require `list_objects`.
Search index lag of up to 30s for newly created issues.
description.parameter_overview: Single `query` string; results returned as smart IDs of the form linear-prod-linear:object:Issue:LIN-1234 or linear-prod-linear:object:Project:proj_uuid, ranked by relevance and recency.

query.description: Free-text search query (issue title, identifier, or label substring).

truncation.guidance_template: Showing {N} of {Total} matches. Use `cursor` to paginate or refine your query (e.g. add team identifier prefix LIN-).

description.purpose: Fetch the full Linear object addressed by a smart ID (Issue, Project, or Cycle).
when_to_use: When you have a smart ID returned by `search` or `list_objects`.
When you need the full property set, comments, or sub-tasks of an issue.
limitations: Comments and attachments are returned as a separate property; agents must request explicitly via `properties`.
Returns 404 if the object was deleted or never existed.
description.parameter_overview: Single `id` string in the smart-ID format `linear-prod-linear:object:{Issue|Project|Cycle}:{identifier}`; routing maps the type to the correct GraphQL query.

truncation.guidance_template: Issue exceeded {threshold} tokens; {N} fields included. Re-call with `properties` projection (e.g. drop `description` for issues with long bodies).

description.purpose: List the Linear teams, projects, and cycles the integration has access to (each is a collection of issues).
when_to_use: At session start to discover what teams the user can read.
When mapping a free-text request to a specific team or cycle id.
limitations: Only collections shared with the integration's API key are visible.
Returns metadata only — use `list_objects` to enumerate issues within a collection.
description.parameter_overview: Optional `pattern` (glob on team/project name) and `include_schema` (bool) for embedding the issue-state schema; defaults return all visible collections without schema.

truncation.guidance_template: Listed {N} collections. Use `pattern` to narrow by name.

description.purpose: List Linear issues within a chosen team, project, or cycle with filter, sort, projection, and cursor pagination.
when_to_use: When enumerating issues in a known team or cycle.
When server-side filter (e.g., state=Todo, assignee=user_id) or sort by priority is needed.
when_not_to_use: When you have an explicit issue identifier — use `fetch`.
When the team or cycle id is unknown — use `search` or `list_collections` first.
limitations: Cursor pagination only; max 100 issues per call (Linear GraphQL cap).
Filter expressions limited to Linear's documented filter shape (property/operator/value).
Sort restricted to indexed properties (priority, createdAt, updatedAt, identifier).

truncation.guidance_template: Returned {N} of approximately {Total} issues. Use `cursor` to paginate or `properties` to project fewer fields (drop `description` first).

description.purpose: Create a new Linear issue or update an existing one (smart routing by id presence).
when_to_use: When filing a new issue from an external trigger.
When patching state, priority, or assignee on an existing issue.
limitations: Cannot upsert into a Project or Cycle directly — only Issue objects.
Required fields on create: `team` and `title`; mismatches fail with 400.
Re-creating with the same external title produces a duplicate — Linear has no server-side deduplication.
description.parameter_overview: `collection` is the team id. Provide `data.title` and `data.team` for create; `id` + `data` for partial update. Workflow state transitions enforce Linear's per-team state machine.

truncation.guidance_template: {action} succeeded for issue {id}. Refetch with `fetch` if full payload was truncated.

description.purpose: Hard-delete a Linear issue (admin-only). For archival use `issues_archive` instead — Linear treats archive as the soft-delete equivalent.
when_to_use: When permanently removing a test issue from a sandbox team.
When the API key has admin scope and a hard delete is explicitly required.
limitations: Requires admin scope on the API key; will 403 for non-admin tokens.
Hard delete is irreversible. Most callers want `issues_archive` instead.
Re-deleting a deleted issue is a no-op (idempotent).
description.parameter_overview: `type: 'object'` + `id` (smart ID of Issue) + `confirm: true`. Batch delete supported via `ids` array.

truncation.guidance_template: Deleted {deleted_count} of {requested} issues. Failures listed in `failed` array (most often: insufficient scope).

description.purpose: Create a Linear issue and simultaneously link it to parent/blocking/related issues in a single call.
when_to_use: When filing a sub-task that has a known parent issue.
When the new issue blocks or is blocked by existing issues that should be linked atomically.
when_not_to_use: When relations are not known at creation time — use `upsert` to create, then patch relations separately.
When creating multiple unrelated issues — call `upsert` per issue.
limitations: Maximum 10 relations per call (Linear GraphQL mutation cost cap).
Each related issue must already exist; non-existent relation ids fail the entire mutation atomically.
Re-running with the same input creates a duplicate issue (not idempotent).
description.parameter_overview: Required: `team`, `title`. Optional: `description`, `parent_id`, `blocks` (array of issue ids), `blocked_by` (array), `related` (array). All relation arrays accept Linear identifiers (LIN-123) or smart IDs.

truncation.guidance_template: Issue created with {relations_created} relations. Fetch with `fetch` for full payload.

description.purpose: Archive a Linear issue (soft-delete). Linear's canonical removal operation — preferred over `delete` for non-admin callers.
when_to_use: When closing out a completed cycle's issues without losing history.
When sweeping stale issues from a triage queue.
limitations: Re-archiving an archived issue is a no-op (idempotent).
Archived issues remain queryable via `list_objects` with `filter.property=archivedAt,operator=neq,value=null`.
Cannot archive an issue with open sub-tasks; archive sub-tasks first.
description.parameter_overview: Required: `id` (smart ID or LIN-identifier). Optional: `cascade_subtasks` (bool, default false) to archive children.

truncation.guidance_template: Issue {id} archived. Restore via `upsert` with `data.archived: false`.

description.purpose: Advance the active Linear cycle for a team — close the current cycle and open the next sequential cycle.
when_to_use: When a sprint/cycle ends and the next should begin atomically.
When automating cycle rollover from a scheduled trigger.
when_not_to_use: When merely closing a cycle without opening a new one — use `upsert` with cycle.completedAt.
Mid-cycle (Linear rejects the mutation if the active cycle is not within its scheduled close window).
limitations: Requires admin scope.
Advancing twice in the same period creates an empty intermediate cycle (not idempotent).
Open issues in the closing cycle move to the new cycle automatically per team setting.

truncation.guidance_template: Cycle advanced for team {team_id}; {issues_moved} open issues moved to new cycle.
